chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the use of the siwak (tooth-stick) for the fasting person. He said: 'He may use it at any hour he wishes, from the beginning of the day until its end.'

key_terms.السِّوَاك: Tooth-stick used for oral hygiene and religious practice

ai.seo_question: Can a fasting person use siwak during the day in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the permissibility of using the siwak during fasting is established as unrestricted throughout the day, reflecting the general principle that acts of purification do not invalidate the fast. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it aligns with the view that siwak is a recommended act (mustahabb) that does not require specific timing, distinguishing it from other acts like eating or drinking. The chain of transmission highlights the scholarly continuity from Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir) through the reliable narrators of the Tusi school.
